messages:
tyler: Heads up — we've got a p99 spike on host-side for the streaming endpoint after the kernel-selection change yesterday. It looks small in tokens/sec but shows up as extra CPU in the tokenization/parse path.

sophie: Can you paste the traces? is it only streaming or regular generate too? :thinking_face:

tyler: Streaming only so far. Regular generate steady. Link to traces: https://go/perf/dash/host-stream-1961 (internal)

maria: I ran a short replay on canary and saw a ~12% CPU increase on ingress processes. Flamegraph points to two things: 1) gRPC proto parsing spend went up due to more small frames, 2) tokenizer stamping (utf8 normalize) hot path.

kevin: That matches the profiler I ran — kernel selection started preferring a mini-batched kernel for short seqs which increases the number of small writes and triggers extra copy+parse.

alex: Reproducer (small):
```
# send 1k small streaming requests
for i in $(seq 1 1000); do
  echo -n "$(printf 'a%.0s' {1..40})" | grpc_stream --insecure --chunk-size=64
done
```

Results: host ingress CPU up ~1.1x, p99 up 90ms

perf-bot: CI perf job: streaming-host-ingress: baseline=80ms p99, head=170ms p99 (+112.5%), allocations +20% (see job/8793)

sophie: Oof. Two angles: revert kernel policy for short sequences OR address host-side coalescing. Which is cheaper?

kevin: Temporarily reverting kernel choice reduces p99 back to baseline in the replay. But that loses some throughput for mixed workloads. I think we can mitigate host overhead: implement writev coalescing for small frames in the proxy, and collapse duplicate UTF8 normalization calls in tokenizer (we're normalizing twice now due to the new preflight).

maria: I measured KV cache behavior too — more fragmentation in kvcache lookup keys because each tiny frame caused independent cache misses. Batching those lookups (micro-batch window 5–10ms) reduced backend RPCs by ~18%.

tyler: Steps proposed: 1) revert kernel selection on canary (hotfix), 2) land proxy writev coalescing + tokenizer dedupe, 3) add micro-batch window to kvcache lookup as a config flag, 4) run 24h canary with perf probes.

alex: I'll open small PRs: proxy coalesce (rust) and tokenizer fast-path. Will include microbench results.

kevin: I'll prepare the rollback CL. @sophie can you own the canary run and dashboards?

sophie: Yep — will run canary and collect pprof + flamegraphs. Will also test for regressions on long-seq throughput.

maria: Note for rollout: add metric for "ingress_writev_chunks" and kvcache micro-batch hits so we can track before/after without digging traces.

tyler: Good. Timeline: rollback CL in 30m, proxy+tokenizer PRs today, canary infra + metrics tomorrow morning. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
